title: Pluggable kernel adapters for on-demand CUTLASS/Triton bindings
creator: Asha Patel
description: This ticket standardizes a pluggable kernel adapter layer that allows the runtime to lazily bind to CUTLASS and Triton kernels on-demand per model, and to perform deterministic symbol isolation. Goals: reduce cold-start probe jitter, enable binary-delta rollouts for kernel bundles, and provide a safe runtime fallback path for heterogeneous fleets. The adapter introduces a small stable API surface for kernel lookup, and a loading policy that supports canary/diff rollouts and A/B kernel selection by model tag.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime can load CUTLASS/Triton kernel bundles on-demand without full process restart
Symbol namespace isolation prevents CLASH for two different CUTLASS versions loaded in the same process
Canary rollout flow (binary-delta) successfully routes 5% traffic to new kernel bundle and automatically rolls back on perf regression
End-to-end latency variance for model cold-start reduced by >=20% in synthetic microbench
Integration tests covering fallback path (fallback to dev-build or CPU path) pass in CI and on a dedicated canary pool
steps: Design adapter API and permutation registry (interface doc in Confluence)
Implement loader with dlmopen/dlopen variants and namespace sandboxing
Create binary-delta packaging script and artifact verifier (signed bundles)
Add canary routing hooks to scheduler and Dedicated capacity controller
Instrument telemetry: kernel-load durations, symbol conflicts, per-model kernel metric
Add integration tests for mixed-version load and CI gates for new kernel artifacts

notes_and_tradeoffs: Tradeoff: dlmopen provides namespace isolation but complicates signal handling and increases memory usage due to duplicate libraries. We accept modest memory overhead for improved isolation on Dedicated pools.
Decision: use binary-delta artifacts rather than full rebuilds to speed rollout and reduce network egress. Requires strict artifact signing and CI gating.

Fallback strategy: if adapter fails to load a kernel bundle for a model, scheduler will automatically route to a compatible pinned model variant or fall back to CPU/quantized path for best-effort availability.
Edge-case: global singletons in Triton/CUTLASS may need shimming. We will use a shim layer that exposes a stable symbol facade; follow-up tickets will encapsulate model-specific patches.
